title: Quiet Errands
tagline: A few chores close to home that turn out to matter.
opening: It begins small, the way these things do. A few errands, and a feeling that they are not as idle as they seem.
ending: The errands are done, and the land is a little safer for them. Small things, rightly done, add up.

steps.tell: First, the simple part: {area} holds what we need, and the rest of what follows depends on it. Bring it together.
Next, someone must see for themselves what has become of a place in {area}. Go, look, and carry back the truth.
What you saw was no accident. Whatever is stirring in {area} must be put down before it spreads.

title: The Long Road
tagline: A journey out through the lands, with trouble at every stop.
opening: A road runs out of here through the lands, and every stop along it holds a task. Walk it to the end.
ending: The road is walked, and those who walked it are not the ones who set out.

steps.tell: The road begins in {area}. Go there first and see what waits. Nobody has been that way in some time.
The road is not safe. In {area}, creatures have claimed it. Clear them, and travellers can pass again.
Beyond {from} lies {area}, where what we need grows. Take it, and the road pays for itself.
At the road's end, in {area}, something old lies hidden. Find it, and the journey will have meant something.

title: The Great Hunt
tagline: Drive the danger back, land by land, to its source.
opening: A threat has been spreading from land to land. Follow it back to where it began, and do not stop until it does.
ending: The hunt is over. Whatever drove the beasts has gone quiet, and the lands breathe again.

steps.tell: It starts here, in {area}. Thin their numbers, then follow where they flee.
They have run to {area}, and they are angrier. Bring them down before they dig in.
Now {area}. Whatever is leading them is near. Deal with those around it first.
Their trail ends in {area}. Reach the place where it stops, and be ready for what you find.

title: A Harvest Against the Dark
tagline: Gather what the lands hold, while something stalks the gatherers.
opening: The lands still give, if you know where to look, and something has noticed. Gather fast, and gather together.
ending: The harvest is in. It will keep the settlements through the dark, and that is all anyone asked.

steps.tell: The nearest of it grows here in {area}. Take what you can carry and keep your guard up.
Something follows the gatherers. In {area} it has gone from watching to hunting. End it.
More grows in {area}, past where the stalker lurked. Take it too.

title: The Lost Relics
tagline: Three old things, scattered across the lands, each worth a story.
opening: Three things were hidden long ago in three different lands. Each is worth finding. Together, they are worth more.
ending: All three are found. Whatever they were made for, they will not sit in the dark any longer.

steps.tell: The first lies somewhere in {area}. The old stories say it glows when someone worthy is near.
The second is in {area}. It has had longer to be forgotten, so it will be harder to see.
The third lies in {area}, farthest of all. If you have come this far, you will know what to look for.

title: Pilgrimage to the Far Shrine
tagline: A long walk to a far place, with the lands watching.
opening: There is a shrine at the far edge of the world, and a long, patient way to get there. Walk it with care.
ending: The shrine is reached, and the long walk is over. Rest now. You have earned the quiet.

steps.tell: The pilgrimage starts in {area}. Go there and begin.
Then {area}. The way is longer than it looks, and the land does not care that you are tired.
On to {area}. Others have turned back here. Do not.
The shrine is guarded in {area}. Clear the way, and you will be let in.

title: The Siege of the Frontier
tagline: Hold the line, then carry the fight out into the wild.
opening: The frontier is under siege and the settlements are calling for help. Break the siege, then take the fight to those behind it.
ending: The siege is broken, and those who laid it are scattered. The frontier will hold for now.

steps.tell: The first wave has reached {area}. Break it, or there will be nothing left to defend.
We need supplies to hold out. They grow in {area}. Bring them back, quickly.
A second wave is gathering in {area}. Strike it while it is still forming.
The leaders are in {area}. Bring them down and the rest will break.
In {area} they dropped what they came for. Find it, so they cannot come back for it.

title: Beyond the Edge of the Map
tagline: Into the farthest lands, where nobody has gone and returned.
opening: Past the lands everyone knows are the lands almost nobody does. Go as far as the paths go, and then a little farther.
ending: You have gone farther than anyone, and come back. That is worth a story, and you will tell it well.

steps.tell: Start in {area}, where the maps begin to thin. Reach the place at its heart.
In {area}, things grow that grow nowhere else. Gather them: the proof will be needed.
The farthest land, {area}, is no longer empty. Whatever lives there does not welcome visitors.
At the very edge of {area} there is something left by whoever came here first. Find it.

title: The Hollow Crown
tagline: A king's lost regalia, a trail of grave-robbers, a long reckoning.
opening: A crown was stolen, and with it, the right to rule. Follow the trail wherever it goes. Nobody who followed it has returned.
ending: The crown is found, and the trail is closed. What happens to it next is a story for another day.

steps.tell: The first piece of the regalia is hidden in {area}. The thieves did not think anyone would look there.
In {area}, the thieves have made a camp and set guards. Break it.
Their trail leads to {area}. Reach the place where it ends, and see who waits.
There are too many in {area} to simply walk past. Fight through.
The crown itself is somewhere in {area}. After all this, you will know it when you see it.

title: The Lost Courier
tagline: A sealed letter, three strangers and a message that must arrive.
opening: A letter was given to a courier, and the courier never arrived. Somebody, somewhere, is still waiting for it. Let us see who.
ending: The letter reached the hand it was meant for, and the world is a little less lost for it.

postmaster.name: Aldis the Postmaster
lines: No courier has come through in days. I fear the worst.
If you find the letter, do not open it.

courier.name: Wren the Courier
lines: I ran. I am not proud of it, but I ran.
Take the letter. Take it to the one it was meant for.

reader.name: Sage Orrin
lines: Letters from the old road. Rare, these days.
Whoever sent this knew more than they wrote.

steps.tell: The postmaster in {area} is beside himself. Find Aldis, and hear what happened.
says: A courier left here three days ago with a sealed letter, and has not been seen since.
She was last bound for the lands beyond. Find her, if you can, and the letter with her.

steps.tell: Whatever stopped the courier is still out there in {area}. Clear the road before you follow it.
A frightened traveller is hiding in {area}. Find Wren the courier.
says: You came for the letter. Good. I could not carry it another step.
It is for the old sage who keeps the lore. Please, see it into their hands.

steps.tell: The sage the letter is for lives in {area}. Carry the Sealed Letter there and give it over.
says: Ah. So it has come at last. You have done more than you know.
What it says is not for you, but this I will tell you: the roads will be safer for it.

title: The Silent Bell
tagline: A bell that stopped ringing, a keeper with a secret, a trail to follow.
opening: There was a bell in the lands that rang every dusk. It has gone silent, and the silence has begun to spread.
ending: The bell rang again at dusk, and everyone who heard it knew the long silence was over.

ringer.name: Old Maren the Ringer
lines: Forty years I rang that bell. Now there is only quiet.
Find what took the clapper, and bring it home.

smith.name: Dorrin Ashhand
lines: I mend what breaks, but I cannot mend what is missing.
Bring me the clapper and the bell will sing.

steps.tell: The bell-ringer in {area} has a sorrow to tell. Find Old Maren.
says: The bell hangs there still, but its voice is gone. The clapper was taken in the night.
Whoever took it left tracks heading out. Follow them.

steps.tell: The tracks end in {area}. The clapper is hidden somewhere near. Search the land until you have it.
Whatever carried it off has made its den in {area}, and it will not give the clapper up without a fight.
Take the clapper to the smith in {area}. Find Dorrin Ashhand.
says: A fine piece, and nearly whole. Give me a moment at the anvil.
There. Carry it back to the bell, and may it ring true.

steps.tell: The bell hangs where it always did, in {area}. Return the clapper to it, and let it ring.

title: The Wanderer's Debt
tagline: A stranger owes a favour to someone he has never met, and you are the road between.
opening: A wanderer on the road owes a debt he cannot pay. Perhaps you can pay it for him, and learn something on the way.
ending: The debt is paid, the wanderer is free, and two strangers parted as friends.

wanderer.name: Corwin the Wanderer
lines: I owe someone a debt, and I do not even know their face.
They live beyond the next land, so I am told.

creditor.name: Keeper Hale
lines: A debt? I had forgotten it entirely.
Odd, to be repaid by strangers.

steps.tell: A traveller in {area} is looking for help with a debt. Find Corwin.
says: Take these coins, friends. They are what I owe, and a little more.
The one I owe lives some way off. Please, find them. I cannot.

steps.tell: On the road to the creditor, {area} offers what a gift ought to have beside it. Gather it as you pass.
The creditor is in {area}. Find Keeper Hale, and settle the debt.
says: These are the old coins, aren't they? My grandmother's pouch.
Tell Corwin the debt is paid, and something more besides. He is welcome at my fire.
